item.title: China to expand cooperation with Singapore in technology, digital economy, AI, green industry: Chinese vice premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
SINGAPORE, Nov. 23 -- China is willing to work with Singapore to upgrade cooperation in traditional fields, and expand cooperation in emerging fields such as technological innovation, the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI), and green industries, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said Monday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, met with Singaporean Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong in Singapore. They also co-chaired the 22nd China-Singapore Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation Meeting, the 27th China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park Joint Steering Council Meeting, the 18th China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Joint Steering Council Meeting, and the 10th China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity Joint Steering Council Meeting. Ding said that the practical cooperation between China and Singapore has achieved remarkable results, reflecting the all-round high-quality future-oriented nature of bilateral relations. Against a complex international backdrop, both sides should build on past successes, adapt to changing circumstances, seize new opportunities and explore new avenues for cooperation to support their respective modernization efforts, he said. China stands ready to work with Singapore to implement the important consensus reached by the two countries' leaders, make full use of the role of intergovernmental cooperation in driving broader collaboration, and explore ways to better align China's 15th Five-Year Plan with Singapore's national development priorities, Ding said. Gan said that Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had just visited China, during which he had productive exchanges with Chinese leaders on Singapore-China relations, providing direction for bilateral cooperation. Singapore is willing to work with China to explore ways to make better use of mechanisms and intergovernmental projects, deepen cooperation in such fields as the digital economy, AI, the services sector and connectivity, and deliver more practical results under the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, said Gan. The meetings yielded 29 outcomes in emerging and frontier areas, financial cooperation, health and other fields.

item.title: Xi's speech marking 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth published
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
BEIJING, Nov. 23 -- A speech delivered by Chinese President Xi Jinping at a ceremony marking the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth has been published as a booklet. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the speech in Beijing on Nov. 12. The booklet, published by the People's Publishing House, is now available at Xinhua Bookstore outlets nationwide.

item.title: China vows to foster stable environment for business cooperation with Australia: premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 20 -- China stands ready to work with Australia to eliminate disruptions to normal economic and trade exchanges, and provide a favorable environment and stable expectations for business cooperation between the two countries, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Friday. Li made the remarks while jointly attending the 9th China-Australia CEO Roundtable with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Li said China-Australia relations and cooperation have made considerable new progress over the past year under the strategic guidance of the leaders of the two countries. These hard-won achievements came amid severe disruptions to international trade and sluggish global economic growth, fully demonstrating the strong inherent momentum of bilateral cooperation, he said. Practice has repeatedly shown that China and Australia have highly complementary economic strengths and extensive common interests, making them natural partners for cooperation and opportunities for each other's development, Li added. Noting that global development still faces many uncertainties, Li said that stable and reliable partners are all the more important in times of uncertainty. China and Australia should further strengthen economic and trade ties to achieve broader and higher-level mutually beneficial cooperation, he said. Li called on the two sides to deepen cooperation in three key areas. First, the two countries should focus on consumption upgrading to improve people's quality of life. While consolidating and expanding traditional trade in agricultural and food products, they should tap the potential for cooperation in tourism, education, healthcare and elderly care, biomedicine and high-end medical services, and develop more high-quality products and services to meet people's needs throughout their lives. Second, the two sides should strengthen innovation cooperation, particularly in digital and intelligent technologies. They should better integrate their respective strengths in innovation, enhance mutual empowerment and deepen cooperation in the application and industrialization of new technologies, so as to accelerate the transformation of research achievements into new products and orders for businesses in both countries and better share the benefits of innovation. Third, the two countries should deepen cooperation in green and low-carbon transition for sustainable development. They should jointly develop competitive green products, build green steel supply chains and new energy vehicle industrial and supply chains, explore third-party markets together, and move up the global green value chain. Li stressed that the Chinese government stands ready to work with the Australian government to keep bilateral relations in the right direction, maintain win-win cooperation as the prevailing trend, and eliminate disruptions to normal economic and trade exchanges, so as to provide a favorable environment and stable expectations for business cooperation. China's door to the outside world will only open wider, and more Australian companies are welcome to deepen their presence in the Chinese market, Li said. He expressed hope that the business communities of both countries would continue to serve as pioneers of mutually beneficial cooperation and promoters of bilateral friendship, and help achieve new results in China-Australia economic and trade cooperation. Albanese said China is Australia's largest trading partner, and that bilateral economic and trade cooperation contributes to the economic development of both countries and brings tangible benefits to their peoples. Noting that next year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Australia and China, Albanese said Australia stands ready to take this opportunity to strengthen mutually beneficial cooperation with China in areas such as artificial intelligence, green transition and modern agriculture, and deepen people-to-people and cultural exchanges. He expressed hope that the business communities of the two countries would learn from each other, draw on each other's experiences, expand cooperation, and make greater contributions to the development of Australia-China relations.

item.title: China ready to accelerate FTA upgrade talks with Singapore: premier
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 -- China stands ready to work with Singapore to accelerate negotiations on the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) 4.0 and promote a higher level of two-way opening-up, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said Saturday. Li made the remarks during talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Beijing. Li said China is willing to strengthen strategic communication with Singapore, consolidate political mutual trust, support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, and expand practical cooperation. The two sides should strive for more achievements in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership and continuously improve the well-being of the two peoples, Li said. Li called on the two sides to further strengthen industrial integration, upgrade major bilateral government-to-government cooperation projects, and deepen cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, clean energy, connectivity and finance. The two countries should also advance the development of the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor to inject fresh impetus into their development, he said. Noting that China and Singapore share similar approaches to social governance and face many common challenges, Li called for greater exchanges and mutual learning to address population aging, promote balanced development and improve public services. The two sides should also expand people-to-people and cultural cooperation in areas such as tourism, culture and youth exchanges, he added. Li said China and Singapore should forge closer coordination and cooperation within the United Nations, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and other relevant frameworks, firmly promote regional economic integration, advance the building of an open world economy, uphold the multilateral trading system and safeguard their common interests. China supports Singapore in assuming the rotating chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next year, and stands ready to work with Singapore to encourage all parties to implement the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol effectively, Li said. Wong congratulated China on successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen. He said Singapore and China have built a strong partnership based on deep mutual trust over the past decades. Singapore looks forward to maintaining closer high-level exchanges with China, strengthening the alignment of development strategies, deepening cooperation in areas such as artificial intelligence, the digital economy, green energy and connectivity, and enhancing people-to-people and cultural exchanges, Wong said. Singapore stands ready to work with China to achieve more results in their all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership, he added. Wong said Singapore supports the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four global initiatives proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, and appreciates China's leadership in maintaining world peace and promoting openness and development.

item.title: Chinese vice premier urges steadily advancing rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
LANZHOU, Nov. 19 -- Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong has called for consolidating poverty alleviation achievements, preventing large-scale relapse into poverty, and steadily advancing rural revitalization across the board. Liu, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a research tour from Monday to Thursday in northwest China's Gansu Province. He chaired a symposium on regular assistance work in five provinces and autonomous regions in northwest China. In Longnan's Tanchang County, Wenxian County and Wudu District, Liu inspected the monitoring system to prevent relapse into poverty, industrial and employment assistance, east-west collaboration, and targeted assistance by central government agencies. This year marks the first year of implementing regular assistance. Efforts must be made to carry out all related policies and measures in a meticulous and thorough manner, and continue to improve the lives of rural residents, he said. It is necessary to promote the upgrading of assistance industries in accordance with local conditions, strengthen skills training and labor cooperation, and spare no effort to expand employment channels, Liu noted. Also, work should be done to develop the county-level economy and help accelerate the development of old revolutionary base areas, ethnic minority areas and border areas, he said. The vice premier, in addition, stressed applying the experience gained from the Green Rural Revival Program in Zhejiang Province in east China to build a beautiful and harmonious countryside that is desirable to live and work in.

item.title: Chinese vice premier urges joint efforts to boost global silk industry
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
HANGZHOU, Nov. 20 -- Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing on Friday called for joint efforts to promote the prosperity and development of the global silk industry. Zhang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks while addressing the inaugural meeting of the International Network for Silk in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province. Noting that silk serves as an important vehicle for jointly building the Belt and Road Initiative and promoting economic and trade ties and cultural exchanges, Zhang said China's silk industry has made rapid progress in technological innovation, industrial ecosystem development and brand building in recent years. He expressed China's readiness to work with other countries to implement the four global initiatives and carry forward the Silk Road spirit of peace and cooperation, openness and inclusiveness, mutual learning and mutual benefit to promote the prosperity of the global silk industry. Zhang urged efforts to establish a public service platform under the International Network for Silk for information sharing, matching supply with demand and facilitating practical cooperation in areas including sericulture, processing, trade and investment. He also called for making full use of the International Network for Silk as a cooperation platform to develop the industry, facilitate trade and preserve cultural heritage, thereby injecting fresh impetus into high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. During his stay in Zhejiang, Zhang also inspected time-honored industries. He called for efforts such as strengthening the preservation and innovation of these industries, enhancing intellectual property protection and utilization, and promoting their integration with culture, tourism, health and wellness, education and rural revitalization to foster new consumption scenarios and growth drivers.

item.title: Xi makes four points on how major countries should get along with each other
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace. Major countries should uphold mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation, Xi said at a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Xi said that countries should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, respect the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and respect each other's core interests and major concerns. They should not interfere in other countries' domestic affairs or each other's internal affairs, he said. On major sensitive issues concerning one another, it is important to communicate in advance, try to see things from one another's perspective, act with caution, and in particular, not to challenge the red lines of one another, Xi said. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among themselves, but should hold the line on peaceful coexistence and make efforts to avoid the Thucydides Trap. As the main victors of World War II, China, Russia and the United States should steadfastly safeguard the postwar international order, Xi said. He said that nuclear weapons, the Sword of Damocles that hangs over humanity, should be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of nuclear weapons. He emphasized the importance of win-win cooperation. The three countries should strengthen economic cooperation and trade, combine their respective strengths as major countries in resources, manufacturing and consumption, so as to make the pie of cooperation bigger and achieve win-win and all-win outcomes. Decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains are not the way to go. Xi said that the three countries could strengthen communication and coordination to safeguard the security and stability of the global energy market. He said that the three countries should maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms to ensure that misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate. Xi said that China, Russia and the United States should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. item.title: Chinese premier signs decree to revise, repeal certain administrative regulations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
BEIJING, Nov. 5 -- A decision by China's State Council to amend and repeal certain administrative regulations was made public on Thursday. Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating the decision, which aims to address pointless formalities to lighten the burden on those working on the ground, implement the reform of Party and state institutions, and ensure the consistency of relevant laws and regulations. Certain provisions of 14 administrative regulations were revised, and four regulations were repealed, according to the document. The State Council decided to revise a regulation on river course administration to align it with related provisions in the country's Ecological and Environmental Code. Meanwhile, a regulation on the limits of liability for maritime passenger transport between Chinese ports was repealed to better meet the needs of ongoing reform and development, and address practical realities in relevant areas. The decision takes effect on the date of its promulgation.
